verdicts.trueWording: boxed text longer than a paragraph probably isn't worth reading
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture fetched 200, 13,874 bytes; quote is word-for-word under the heading 'Undercover Insight #1: Boxed Text = MEGO', introduced as 'My hypothesis was that...' and followed by 'What I actually saw was much more dramatic than my hypothesis' - so the prior-hypothesis limb is explicit. The first-person narrator of that section is Noonan: the column later calls the method 'Dave wanders around' and asks whether adventures change 'because Dave spent a lot of time wandering around'.

verdicts.trueWording: Boxed text replaces that conversation with oration.
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the same page. The antecedent is supplied two paragraphs earlier ('At its heart, a D&D game is a conversation'), and the column ranks this above two other factors, naming it 'the conversation vs. oration factor'. Both limbs - that it is his explanation, and that the mechanism is conversation displaced by oration - are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: ditch the boxed text and use your own words
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the closing 'In the meantime' paragraph; the page continues 'for the initial description of the room', which carries the claim's 'describe the room' limb. Attribution limb: the column is co-bylined 'By Jesse Decker and David Noonan', both Wizards R&D staff per the About the Authors block, and the closing section speaks as 'we' - but the advice paragraph itself is in the singular undercover voice, so 'two Wizards designers' rests on the byline, not on a joint first person.

verdicts.trueWording: That's pretty short. Contrast it with the first room
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the 'Tangent Alert!' aside. The 2005 passage quoted (from Sons of Gruumsh, called 'a recent Forgotten Realms adventure' - the page does not date it) is indeed three sentences; the comparator is named as 1999's Return to the Keep on the Borderlands. The contraction limb is the column's own generalisation immediately above the pair - that boxed text used to be much longer than it is today - so it is asserted, not inferred; but it rests on two hand-picked passages, not a corpus measure, and 5th edition is nowhere on the page, so 'before 5th edition' is external chronology (2005 precedes 2014).

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'is an internal PDF ... rather than a published book' - the page never says internal, and states the documents 'are now available for all DMsGuild creators' as a free ($0.00) watermarked PDF download
verdicts.trueWording: distributed by Wizards of the Coast to official play writers
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture fetched 200, 56,942 bytes. Quote verbatim. The January 2019 limb is verbatim too, on its own line above the description: the House Style Guide has been updated January 2019 (the package's File Last Updated is 22 February 2019). The package also bundles adventure-design tips from Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsand, D&D IP guidance and a Forgotten Realms guide, and the page says following them is not required to publish on DMsGuild. 'Internal' is fair as origin but wrong as present access - the cited page is itself a public free download of the guide.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'widely circulated' - the page carries no circulation evidence at all (a personal WordPress blog post with 8 comments); nothing on it speaks to reach
verdicts.trueWording: I was looking for an official writer's guide, or style sheet
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched 200 with a browser UA, 39,307 bytes. Quote verbatim in the opening under 'Style Guide for Dungeon Masters'. The two substantive limbs are verbatim: 'Perhaps they have one and I just couldn't find it' (no official 5e sheet found) and 'So I took the copies I had from 3.5 and 4.0 and updated them for 5th edition' (the back-fit). Author is 'Ronny', posted 3 August 2015, matching the claim's date.

Verbatim as the first line of the 'Tense' section on the same page. The second limb is verbatim on the next line - avoid the future tense 'will' to describe NPC or monster actions - with a worked golem-attacks example. Note the claim's own confidence field is right: this is Ronny's compilation from the 3.5 and 4.0 guides, not a Wizards 5e document, so it is evidence of fan-codified house style, not of Wizards' own rule.

verdicts.trueWording: reduce it down to one or two SIMPLE sentences
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched 200 with a browser UA, 43,692 bytes; post dated 29 September 2013, byline Dyson Logos. Quote verbatim (SIMPLE capitalised in the original). The point-form limb is verbatim in the next sentence, as the preferred option ('But really, replace it with a point-form list of things seen in the room'), and the first option offered is to get rid of boxed text entirely. The relay limb holds: the post names Jesse Decker and David Noonan, block-quotes their Gen Con passage, and links the wizards.com article. One narrowing to flag: the page addresses 'OSR adventure writers', not adventure writers generally.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: '9 paragraphs' - re-measurement of the same PDF gives 21 indent-marked paragraphs (avg 73 words each); 9 is the count of heading-delimited sections. The 'only sustained place-describing prose in the document' limb is also a whole-document judgment over 403 pages that the cited pages cannot establish
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED by re-measurement: PDF re-fetched from media.wizards.com (200, 3,158,713 bytes, sha256 2504d2a0abb0a4d491a939be4f17910a2dde0312570ab8d208080225ccf0a1f0), pdftotext -enc UTF-8, appendix isolated on PDF pages 363-365. Heading 'Appendix PH-C: / The Planes of / Existence' verbatim at the top of p. 363. Body prose (headings and the running head/folio furniture excluded) = 1,530 words excluding the two bold run-in heads 'Spells.' and 'Portals.' (1,532 including them) and 72 sentences - both exact. The 9 corresponds to the intro plus eight headings (The Material Plane, Beyond the Material, Planar Travel, Transitive Planes, Inner Planes, Outer Planes, Outer Planes, Demiplanes).

verdicts.trueWording: mean 21.25 words; population SD 7.54 across 72 sentences
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED by independent re-measurement on the byte-identical PDF: 1,530 body words / 72 sentences = 21.25 -> 21.2, population stdev 7.542 -> 7.5. Counting the two run-in heads instead gives 1,532 words, mean 21.28, population stdev 7.537 - both roundings land on the claim's 21.2 / 7.5 only under the 1,530-word tokenisation, which is the one the claim itself uses. Sample (n-1) stdev would be 7.59, so the claim's 'population' qualifier is load-bearing and correct.

CONFIRMED for the headline and three of four bracket figures. Re-measured min 8 ('Such a journey is the stuff of legend.'), max 41 (the 'Some are vortices...' sentence on p. 363), p10 11, p50 21. One convention caveat, stated visibly rather than buried: p90 re-measures at 30.9 by linear interpolation and 31 by nearest rank, so the claim's p90 30 holds only under a lower/truncating percentile method. Nothing in the appendix falls below 8 words once the run-in heads 'Spells.' and 'Portals.' are attached to their sentences, which is how the 72-sentence count is reached.

CONFIRMED exactly by re-measurement: 8/72 = 11.1111%. The eight are the 33-, 32-, 34-, 35-, 41-, 32-, 31- and 34-word sentences; the 31-word one is the 'guided tour of the Nine Hells' sentence, so the count is sensitive to whether >30 or >=30 is used - >30 is what reproduces 8.

verdicts.trueWording: zero digit characters in the appendix body prose
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED: a regex scan for [0-9] over the 1,530-word body returns nothing. The only digits on pp. 363-365 are page furniture excluded from the body - the running head 'System Reference Document 5.1' and the folios 363, 364, 365 - so the claim is true of the prose and would be false of the raw page text.

verdicts.trueWording: from the first layer to the ninth
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim on p. 364 in the Outer Planes section, matching the claim's page cite; 'sixteen planes' is also verbatim on p. 364. CONFIRMED by the same zero-digit scan: every quantity in the appendix is spelled out - four Elemental Planes, two ways, eight alignments, sixteen, Nine Hells, first, ninth, single.

The 72-sentence numerator reproduces, but the 9-paragraph denominator does not. Re-measurement of the byte-identical PDF finds 21 paragraphs in PH-C, identified by the typographic first-line indents pdftotext preserves plus the first paragraph after each heading: 72/21 = 3.43 sentences and 73 words per paragraph. The 9 is the number of heading-delimited sections (intro plus The Material Plane, Beyond the Material, Planar Travel, Transitive Planes, Inner Planes, Outer Planes, Outer Planes, Demiplanes), so a section count has been reported as a paragraph count and the per-paragraph average is inflated roughly 2.3x. Downstream: do not carry 8.00 sentences per paragraph.
